message.reasoning_content: Answer the judge's contract-scope question (d1). Key facts: problem.txt says "every value is rounded to the nearest representable e4m3 value" with no range restriction; no test.py or get_inputs; artifact holds only kernel.py, meta.json, problem.txt. So the problem text itself is the operative contract, and it imposes the nearest-representable requirement unconditionally on every value. However, I should note the counter-consideration: the contract text describes binade behavior generically ("within any binade it can represent 8 evenly spaced values") without mentioning saturation; the relative-error framing focuses on normals. But "every value" with no domain restriction makes any float32 input in scope; the "nearest representable e4m3 value" for 464 is 448 (since nothing above 448 is representable). So returning 480 violates the explicit requirement. Also note 6.25% relative-error bound claim only holds for normals. Record update with task_id d1 resolved.
